empty.title_idle: Connect to the car to see the check-engine light
empty.p_idle: The app reads the car's trouble codes, explains what they mean and what you can do, and lets you clear the codes to turn the light off.
empty.step1: Plug the ELM327 adapter into the OBD-II port (under the dashboard, driver's side).
empty.step2: Turn the key to ignition ON (position II) or start the engine.
empty.step3: Pair the adapter with your computer (PIN 1234) and click Connect.

hero.sub_mil_no_codes: The ECU did not list codes in this reading
verdict.ok_text: No trouble codes and the light is off.
verdict.noread_title: Light on, but no readable codes
verdict.noread_text: The ECU did not report codes in this reading. Read again and, if it persists, see a workshop with a full scanner.
verdict.1_text: The current codes are low severity. Fix them when you can.
verdict.2_title: You can drive, but fix it soon
verdict.2_text: Nothing indicates immediate risk, but ignoring it can raise fuel use, pollution or cause bigger damage.
verdict.3_text: At least one code is high severity: take the car to a workshop as soon as possible, on a short trip and without heavy throttle.
verdict.4_text: At least one code is critical. Stop in a safe place and call roadside assistance or a workshop.
verdict.flashing: If the light is FLASHING, stop as soon as it is safe.
stale.msg: The number of codes changed since the last reading. Click "Read codes again".
sec.none_stored: No stored codes in the ECU.
sec.pending_hint: have not turned the light on yet
sec.pending_note: The ECU saw the fault once and waits to confirm it on the next trip. If confirmed, it becomes a stored code and the light comes on.
sec.permanent_hint: only go away by themselves after the fault is fixed
sec.freeze: Data at the moment of the fault
sec.freeze_caption: Snapshot from the ECU when code {code} was stored:
sec.freeze_none: No freeze-frame data (or the car does not provide it).
sec.monitors_note: After clearing codes, the monitors reset and the car needs to be driven for a few days (drive cycles) to complete the tests again. If you need an inspection, wait until all of them are ready.
card.freeze_note: This was the fault that stored the freeze-frame data (see "Data at the moment of the fault" below).
card.search: Search this code on the web (needs internet)
dash.no_data: No live data. Connect to the car (or use the demo) to see the instruments.

conn.title: Connect to the car
conn.intro: Before you start: adapter plugged into the car with its LED on, ignition on and the adapter paired (PIN 1234).
conn.auto_none: No adapter port found yet: pair the adapter (Help tab)
conn.car_hint: E.g. Honda Fit 2011. If it contains "Honda", brand-specific tips are shown.
conn.demo_p: A simulated car (fake data) so you can get to know the dashboard.
conn.failed_tips: Tips: is the adapter LED on? Ignition on? Adapter paired? See the Help tab.
clear.title: Clear the codes and turn the check-engine light off?
clear.codes_now: Current codes: {codes}. The app saves a copy in History before clearing.
clear.copy_saved: The app saves a copy of the current reading in History before clearing.
clear.b1: The app sends the "clear codes" command (mode 04) to the ECU. The light goes off if the car accepts it.
clear.b2: Clearing does NOT fix the fault. If it persists, the light comes back (sometimes within minutes, sometimes after a few days of use).
clear.b3: It also resets the freeze-frame data and the readiness monitors: the car needs to be driven for a few days to complete them again (important before an emissions inspection).
clear.b4: Do it with the ignition on. If the ECU refuses while the engine is running, switch the engine off (key to ON) and try again.
clear.ack: I understand: I noted/saved the codes and I know the light can come back if the fault persists.
clear.working_p: Sending the command to the ECU and checking the result (a few seconds).
clear.refused_title: The ECU did not clear the codes
clear.ok_title: Done: the check-engine light is off
clear.ok_note: If the fault persists, the light comes back and the app will show the code again. The copy from before is in the History tab.
clear.still_title: Command accepted, but the light still shows as on
clear.still_codes: There are still codes: {codes}. This means the fault is permanent or came back right away.
clear.still_nocodes: The ECU no longer lists codes. The light may take a moment to go off.
toast.report_copied: Report copied. Paste it into a chat or forum to ask for help.
err.server_lost: Could not reach the program on the computer (was its window closed?).
diag.running: Checking the system (can take up to 1 minute)…
diag.hint_nearby: If your adapter (e.g. OBDII) shows up under "nearby", the computer can see it: the problem is only the pairing.
help.before.title: Before you start
help.before.1: Plug the adapter into the car's OBD-II port (under the dashboard on the driver's side, near the brake pedal). The adapter's LED should light up.
help.before.2: Switch the ignition on (key to position II, engine running or not). With the ignition off the car's ECU does not answer.
help.win.title: Pairing on Windows
help.win.1: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Devices. Under Device settings, set Bluetooth devices discovery to Advanced (the default list in Windows 11 hides generic devices such as the ELM327).
help.win.2: Click Add device → Bluetooth, wait about 10 seconds and choose OBDII (or OBD II, V-LINK, ELM327). If it asks for a PIN, type 1234 (some use 0000, 6789 or 1111).
help.win.3: Still not listed? Press Win + R, type control printers and use Add a device: that older wizard shows more devices.
help.win.4: Click Connect here and keep Automatic: the app finds the COM port that Windows creates for the adapter.
help.win.5: No COM port? Windows → More Bluetooth settings → COM Ports tab → Add → Outgoing → pick the OBDII device. Then click Refresh list.
help.linux.title: Pairing on Linux
help.linux.1: Pair with your desktop's Bluetooth settings or in a terminal: bluetoothctl → scan on → pair AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF (PIN 1234) → trust AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
help.linux.2: Click Connect and keep Automatic: paired adapters are used directly through an RFCOMM socket, no root needed. Alternative: sudo rfcomm bind 0 AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF and pick /dev/rfcomm0.
help.linux.3: USB adapters show up as /dev/ttyUSB0. If you get "permission denied", join the group: sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER and log out and in again.
help.fail.title: If it does not connect
help.fail.1: "Access denied" or "timed out": adapter without power (LED off), ignition off, adapter too far from the computer or another program using the port. Close other OBD apps and try again.
help.fail.2: Connected, but "the car is not answering": switch the ignition on (position II) or start the engine. In some cars the ECU only answers with the key in the ON position.
help.fail.3: The adapter is not in the pairing list: use the button below. If it shows up under "nearby", the computer can see it and the problem is only the pairing (see the steps above). If it does not, check the LED and the ignition, and switch off your phone's Bluetooth so it does not grab the adapter.
help.fail.4: No COM port appears after pairing: some "Bluetooth 4.0" adapters are BLE-only and do not create a COM port on Windows. This version uses classic Bluetooth (SPP). Open a GitHub issue with the diagnostic output.
help.fail.5: Windows with two Bluetooth radios: if one shows an error (for example "Generic Bluetooth Radio"), use the other one.
help.mil.title: About the check-engine light
help.mil.1: What it is: the check-engine light (MIL) comes on when the ECU detects a fault that can increase emissions or damage the engine or the catalytic converter.
help.mil.2: FLASHING light: a severe misfire. Stop as soon as it is safe and avoid accelerating: it can destroy the catalytic converter. Call a mechanic.
help.mil.3: Steady light: something needs fixing. If the car drives normally you can usually drive to the workshop; see the guidance for each code.
help.mil.4: Clearing codes turns the light off but does not fix anything. If the fault continues the light comes back (sometimes within minutes, sometimes after a few days). The app saves a copy of the codes before clearing.
help.mil.5: A code points to a circuit or system, not necessarily to the faulty part. Avoid replacing parts based on the code alone.
help.mil.6: This app is a support tool and does not replace a mechanic's assessment. If in doubt about safety, do not drive.
help.ask.title: Asking for help
help.ask.p: In Diagnosis, click Copy report and paste it into a chat, forum or an email to your workshop: it contains the codes, the data frozen when the fault happened and the sensor values. If something goes wrong with the connection, use Car data → Copy log.
